drivingQuestion: Which blessings are recited on seeing extraordinary sights, and in what sense does earthly kingship mirror the kingship of heaven?
outcomeNote: An aggadic sequence of blessing-rulings, verse expositions and narratives; nothing is refuted, and the two expositions of 'Yours, O Lord, is the greatness' by Rabbi Sheila and by the baraita in Rabbi Akiva's name are left standing side by side.

segments.he: דָּרַשׁ רַב הַמְנוּנָא: הָרוֹאֶה בָּבֶל הָרְשָׁעָה צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ חָמֵשׁ בְּרָכוֹת. רָאָה בָּבֶל, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … שֶׁהֶחֱרִיב בָּבֶל הָרְשָׁעָה״. רָאָה בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … שֶׁהֶחֱרִיב בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הָרָשָׁע״. רָאָה גּוֹב שֶׁל אֲרָיוֹת אוֹ כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … שֶׁעָשָׂה נִסִּים לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה״. רָאָה מַרְקוּלִיס, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … שֶׁנָּתַן אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם לְעוֹבְרֵי רְצוֹנוֹ״. רָאָה מָקוֹם שֶׁנּוֹטְלִין מִמֶּנּוּ עָפָר, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … אוֹמֵר וְעוֹשֶׂה גּוֹזֵר וּמְקַיֵּים״.
segments.en: The Gemara goes on to discuss special blessings instituted by the Sages to be recited upon seeing extraordinary sights. «Rav Hamnuna taught: One who sees the wicked Babylonia must recite five blessings.» The Gemara elaborates: «One who saw» the ruins of «Babylonia, recites: Blessed…Who destroyed the wicked Babylonia.» «One who saw» the ruins of «Nebuchadnezzar’s house, recites: Blessed…Who destroyed the house of wicked Nebuchadnezzar.» «One who saw the lion’s den» into which Daniel was thrown (see Daniel ch. 6) «or the furnace» into which Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah «were thrown» (see Daniel ch. 3), «recites: Blessed…Who performed miracles for our ancestors in this place.» «One who saw Mercury, recites: Blessed…Who has shown patience to those who violate His will.» «One who saw a place from which earth is taken,» as over the generations earth was taken from certain places and used as fertilizer or for construction in the surrounding areas, «recites: Blessed…Who speaks and acts, decrees and fulfills.»

segments.he: רָבָא כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי חֲמָרֵי דְּשָׁקְלִי עַפְרָא, טָרֵיף לְהוּ יְדָא עַל גַּבַּיְיהוּ, וְאָמַר: רְהוּטוּ צַדִּיקֵי לְמֶעְבַּד רְעוּתָא דְמָרַיְיכוּ. מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא כִּי הֲוָה מָטֵי לְבָבֶל הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל עַפְרָא בְּסוּדָרֵיהּ וְשָׁדֵי לְבַרָּא, לְקַיֵּים מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְטֵאטֵאתִיהָ בְּמַטְאֲטֵא הַשְׁמֵד״. אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲנָא, הָא דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי, אֶלָּא מִדַּעְתַּאי בָּרֵיכְתִּינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «when Rava would see donkeys carrying earth» from Babylonia, «he would slap their backs with his hand and say» to them: «Run, righteous ones, and fulfill the will of your Master. When Mar, son of Ravina, would arrive in Babylonia he would take earth in his kerchief and throw it outside, to fulfill that which is said: “And I will sweep it with the broom of destruction”» (Isaiah 14:23). «Rav Ashi said: I never heard the» statement of «Rav Hamnuna,» that one who sees Babylonia the wicked must recite five blessings. «However, based on my independent reasoning, I recited all of the blessings.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: נִתְקַלְּלָה בָּבֶל — נִתְקַלְּלוּ שְׁכֵנֶיהָ. נִתְקַלְּלָה שׁוֹמְרוֹן — נִתְבָּרְכוּ שְׁכֵנֶיהָ: נִתְקַלְּלָה בָּבֶל — נִתְקַלְּלוּ שְׁכֵנֶיהָ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְשַׂמְתִּיהָ לְמוֹרַשׁ קִפֹּד וְאַגְמֵי מָיִם״. נִתְקַלְּלָה שׁוֹמְרוֹן נִתְבָּרְכוּ שְׁכֵנֶיהָ — דִּכְתִיב: ״וְשַׂמְתִּי שֹׁמְרוֹן לְעִי הַשָּׂדֶה לְמַטָּעֵי כָרֶם וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: With regard to Babylonia, the Gemara cites what «Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:» When «Babylonia was cursed, its neighbors were cursed» along with it. When «Samaria was cursed, its neighbors were blessed.» When «Babylonia was cursed its neighbors were cursed» along with it, «as it is written: “I will also make it a possession for the bittern,» a wading bird, «and pools of water”» (Isaiah 14:23); not only will it be destroyed, but the site will become a habitat for destructive, environmentally harmful creatures. When «Samaria was cursed,» however, «its neighbors were blessed, as it is written: “Therefore I will make Samaria a heap in the field, a place for the planting of vineyards”» (Micah 1:6); although destroyed, it will serve a beneficial purpose.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: הָרוֹאֶה אוּכְלוּסֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … חֲכַם הָרָזִים״. אוּכְלוּסֵי גּוֹיִם, אוֹמֵר: ״בּוֹשָׁה אִמְּכֶם וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: «And Rav Hamnuna said: One who sees multitudes of Israel,» six hundred thousand Jews, «recites: Blessed…Who knows all secrets.» One who sees «multitudes of gentiles recites: “Your mother shall be sore ashamed,» she that bore you shall be confounded; behold, the hindermost of the nations shall be a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert” (Jeremiah 50:12).

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאֶה אוּכְלוּסֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … חֲכַם הָרָזִים״ — שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתָּם דּוֹמָה זֶה לָזֶה, וְאֵין פַּרְצוּפֵיהֶן דּוֹמִים זֶה לָזֶה. בֶּן זוֹמָא רָאָה אוּכְלוּסָא עַל גַּב מַעֲלָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת, אָמַר: ״בָּרוּךְ … חֲכַם הָרָזִים וּבָרוּךְ … שֶׁבָּרָא כׇּל אֵלּוּ לְשַׁמְּשֵׁנִי״.
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a Tosefta: «One who sees multitudes of Israel recites: Blessed…Who knows all secrets.» Why is this? He sees a whole nation «whose minds are unlike each other and whose faces are unlike each other,» and He Who knows all secrets, God, knows what is in each of their hearts. The Gemara relates: «Ben Zoma once saw a multitude [okhlosa] of Israel» while standing «on a stair on the Temple Mount.» He immediately «recited: Blessed…Who knows all secrets and Blessed…Who created all these to serve me.»

segments.he: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר: כַּמָּה יְגִיעוֹת יָגַע אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן עַד שֶׁמָּצָא פַּת לֶאֱכוֹל: חָרַשׁ, וְזָרַע, וְקָצַר, וְעִמֵּר, וְדָשׁ, וְזָרָה, וּבָרַר, וְטָחַן, וְהִרְקִיד, וְלָשׁ, וְאָפָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָכַל. וַאֲנִי מַשְׁכִּים וּמוֹצֵא כׇּל אֵלּוּ מְתוּקָּנִין לְפָנַי. וְכַמָּה יְגִיעוֹת יָגַע אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן עַד שֶׁמָּצָא בֶּגֶד לִלְבּוֹשׁ: גָּזַז, וְלִבֵּן, וְנִפֵּץ, וְטָוָה, וְאָרַג, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מָצָא בֶּגֶד לִלְבּוֹשׁ, וַאֲנִי מַשְׁכִּים וּמוֹצֵא כׇּל אֵלֶּה מְתוּקָּנִים לְפָנַי. כׇּל אוּמּוֹת שׁוֹקְדוֹת וּבָאוֹת לְפֶתַח בֵּיתִי, וַאֲנִי מַשְׁכִּים וּמוֹצֵא כׇּל אֵלּוּ לְפָנַי.
segments.en: Explaining his custom, «he would say: How much effort did Adam the first» man «exert before he found bread to eat:» He «plowed, sowed, reaped, sheaved, threshed, winnowed» in the wind, «separated» the grain from the chaff, «ground» the grain into flour, «sifted, kneaded, and baked and» only «thereafter he ate. And I,» on the other hand, «wake up and find all of these prepared for me.» Human society employs a division of labor, and each individual benefits from the service of the entire world. Similarly, «how much effort did Adam the first» man «exert before he found a garment to wear?» He «sheared, laundered, combed, spun and wove, and» only «thereafter he found a garment to wear. And I,» on the other hand, «wake up and find all of these prepared for me.» Members of «all nations,» merchants and craftsmen, «diligently come to the entrance of my home, and I wake up and find all of these before me.»

segments.he: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר: אוֹרֵחַ טוֹב מַהוּ אוֹמֵר? — כַּמָּה טְרָחוֹת טָרַח בַּעַל הַבַּיִת בִּשְׁבִילִי, כַּמָּה בָּשָׂר הֵבִיא לְפָנַי, כַּמָּה יַיִן הֵבִיא לְפָנַי, כַּמָּה גְּלוּסְקָאוֹת הֵבִיא לְפָנַי, וְכׇל מַה שֶּׁטָּרַח — לֹא טָרַח אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִילִי. אֲבָל אוֹרֵחַ רַע מַהוּ אוֹמֵר? — מַה טּוֹרַח טָרַח בַּעַל הַבַּיִת זֶה? פַּת אַחַת אָכַלְתִּי, חֲתִיכָה אַחַת אָכַלְתִּי, כּוֹס אֶחָד שָׁתִיתִי, כׇּל טוֹרַח שֶׁטָּרַח בַּעַל הַבַּיִת זֶה — לֹא טָרַח אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו.
segments.en: Ben Zoma «would say: A good guest, what does he say? How much effort did the host expend on my behalf, how much meat did» the host «bring before me. How much wine did he bring before me. How many loaves [geluskaot] did he bring before me. All the» effort «that he expended, he expended only for me. However, a bad guest, what does he say? What effort did the host expend? I ate» only «one» piece of «bread, I ate» only «one piece of meat» and «I drank» only «one cup» of wine. «All the effort that the home owner expended he only expended on behalf of his wife and children.»

segments.he: עַל אוֹרֵחַ טוֹב מַהוּ אוֹמֵר? — ״זְכֹר כִּי תַשְׂגִּיא פׇעֳלוֹ אֲשֶׁר שֹׁרְרוּ אֲנָשִׁים״. עַל אוֹרֵחַ רַע כְּתִיב: ״לָכֵן יְרֵאוּהוּ אֲנָשִׁים וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: «With regard to a good guest, what does he say? “Remember that you magnify his work, whereof men have sung”» (Job 36:24); he praises and acknowledges those who helped him. «With regard to a bad guest it is written: “Men do therefore fear him;» he regards not any who are wise of heart” (Job 37:24).

segments.he: ״וְהָאִישׁ בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל זָקֵן בָּא בַאֲנָשִׁים״. אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב זְבִיד, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: זֶה יִשַׁי אֲבִי דָּוִד שֶׁיָּצָא בְּאוּכְלוּסָא, וְנִכְנַס בְּאוּכְלוּסָא, וְדָרַשׁ בְּאוּכְלוּסָא. אָמַר עוּלָּא: נְקִיטִינַן אֵין אוּכְלוּסָא בְּבָבֶל. תָּנָא: אֵין אוּכְלוּסָא פְּחוּתָה מִשִּׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא.
segments.en: On the topic of multitudes, the Gemara cites another verse: «“And the man in the days of Saul was old, and came among men”» (I Samuel 17:12). «Rava, and some say Rav Zevid, and some say Rav Oshaya, said: This» refers to «Yishai, father of David, who» always «went out with multitudes, and entered with multitudes, and taught Torah with multitudes. Ulla said: We hold there is no multitude in Babylonia.» The Sage «taught: A multitude is no fewer than six hundred thousand» people.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאֶה חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אוֹמֵר ״בָּרוּךְ … שֶׁחָלַק מֵחׇכְמָתוֹ לִירֵאָיו״. חַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … שֶׁנָּתַן מֵחׇכְמָתוֹ לְבָשָׂר וָדָם״. הָרוֹאֶה מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ לִירֵאָיו״. מַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … שֶׁנָּתַן מִכְּבוֹדוֹ לְבָשָׂר וָדָם״.
segments.en: «The Sages taught: One who sees the Sages of Israel recites: Blessed…Who has shared of His wisdom with those who revere Him.» One who sees «Sages of the nations of the world recites: Blessed…Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood. One who sees kings of Israel recites: Blessed…Who has shared of His glory with those who revere Him.» One who sees «kings of the» other «nations of the world recites: Blessed…Who has given of His glory to flesh and blood.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְעוֹלָם יִשְׁתַּדֵּל אָדָם לָרוּץ לִקְרַאת מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל. וְלֹא לִקְרַאת מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּלְבַד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לִקְרַאת מַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁאִם יִזְכֶּה — יַבְחִין בֵּין מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One should always strive to run toward kings of Israel» to greet them. «And not only» should he run «toward kings of Israel, but also toward kings of the nations of the world, so that if he will be privileged» to witnesses the glory of the Messiah (Rashi) and the World-to-Come, «he will distinguish between the kings of Israel and the kings of the nations of the world.»

segments.he: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת סַגִּי נְהוֹר הֲוָה. הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְקַבּוֹלֵי אַפֵּי מַלְכָּא, וְקָם אֲזַל בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת. אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַצְבֵי לְנַהְרָא, כַּגְנֵי לְיָיא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תָּא חֲזִי דְּיָדַעְנָא טְפֵי מִינָּךְ. חֲלַף גּוּנְדָּא קַמַּיְיתָא. כִּי קָא אָוְושָׁא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא: אֲתָא מַלְכָּא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לָא קָאָתֵי. חֲלַף גּוּנְדָּא תִּנְיָינָא. כִּי קָא אָוְושָׁא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא: הַשְׁתָּא קָא אָתֵי מַלְכָּא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לָא קָא אָתֵי מַלְכָּא. חָלֵיף תְּלִיתַאי. כִּי קָא שָׁתְקָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: וַדַּאי הַשְׁתָּא אָתֵי מַלְכָּא.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «Rav Sheshet was blind. Everyone was going to greet the king and Rav Sheshet stood up and went along with them. This heretic found him» there and «said to him:» The intact «jugs» go «to the river, where do the broken» jugs «go?» Why is a blind person going to see the king? Rav Sheshet «said to him: Come see that I know more than you» do. «The first troop passed,» and «when the noise grew louder, this heretic said to him: The king is coming. Rav Sheshet said to him:» The king «is not coming. The second troop passed,» and «when the noise grew louder, this heretic said to him: Now the king is coming. Rav Sheshet said to him: The king is not coming. The third» troop «passed,» and «when there was silence, Rav Sheshet said to him: Certainly now the king is coming.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא: מְנָא לָךְ הָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּמַלְכוּתָא דְאַרְעָא כְּעֵין מַלְכוּתָא דִרְקִיעָא, דִּכְתִיב: ״צֵא וְעָמַדְתָּ בָהָר לִפְנֵי ה׳ וְהִנֵּה ה׳ עֹבֵר וְרוּחַ גְּדוֹלָה וְחָזָק מְפָרֵק הָרִים וּמְשַׁבֵּר סְלָעִים לִפְנֵי ה׳ לֹא בָרוּחַ ה׳ וְאַחַר הָרוּחַ רַעַשׁ לֹא בָרַעַשׁ ה׳. וְאַחַר הָרַעַשׁ אֵשׁ לֹא בָאֵשׁ ה׳ וְאַחַר הָאֵשׁ קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה״.
segments.en: «This heretic said to him: How do you know this?» Rav Sheshet «said to him: Royalty on earth is like royalty in the heavens, as it is written» with regard to God’s revelation to Elijah the Prophet on Mount Horeb: «“And He said: Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord.» «And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and broke in pieces the rocks before the Lord;» «but the Lord was not in the wind;» «and after the wind an earthquake;» «but the Lord was not in the earthquake;» «and after the earthquake a fire;» «but the Lord was not in the fire;» «and after the fire a still small voice.» And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle and went out, and stood in the entrance of the cave” (I Kings 19:11–13). God’s revelation was specifically at the moment of silence.

segments.he: כִּי אֲתָא מַלְכָּא, פָּתַח רַב שֵׁשֶׁת וְקָא מְבָרֵךְ לֵיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא: לְמַאן דְּלָא חָזֵית לֵיהּ קָא מְבָרְכַתְּ? וּמַאי הֲוִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּהָהוּא מִינָא? אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: חַבְרוֹהִי כַּחְלִינְהוּ לְעֵינֵיהּ, וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת נָתַן עֵינָיו בּוֹ, וְנַעֲשָׂה גַּל שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת.
segments.en: «When the king came, Rav Sheshet began to bless him. The heretic» mockingly «said to him: Do you bless someone you do not see?» The Gemara asks: «And what ultimately happened to this heretic? Some say» that «his friends gouged out his eyes, and some say» that «Rav Sheshet fixed his gaze upon him, and» the heretic «became a pile of bones.»

segments.he: רַבִּי שֵׁילָא נַגְּדֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּבְעַל גּוֹיָה. אֲזַל אֲכַל בֵּיהּ קוּרְצֵי בֵּי מַלְכָּא, אֲמַר: אִיכָּא חַד גַּבְרָא בִּיהוּדָאֵי דְּקָא דָּיֵין דִּינָא בְּלָא הַרְמָנָא דְמַלְכָּא. שַׁדַּר עֲלֵיהּ פְּרִיסְתְּקָא. כִּי אֲתָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא נַגֵּדְתֵּיהּ לְהַאי? אֲמַר לְהוּ: דְּבָא עַל חֲמָרְתָא. אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אִית לְךָ סָהֲדִי? אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִין. אֲתָא אֵלִיָּהוּ אִדְּמִי לֵיהּ כְּאִינִישׁ, וְאַסְהֵיד. אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא! אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנַן מִיּוֹמָא דִּגְלֵינַן מֵאַרְעִין לֵית לַן רְשׁוּתָא לְמִקְטַל. אַתּוּן, מַאי דְּבָעֵיתוּן עֲבִידוּ בֵּיהּ.
segments.en: As for the connection between divine and earthly royalty, the Gemara cites another story: «Rabbi Sheila» ordered that «a man who had relations with a gentile woman be flogged.» That man «went to inform the king and said: There is one man among the Jews who renders judgment without the king’s authority [harmana].» The king «sent a messenger [peristaka] for» Rabbi Sheila to bring him to trial. «When» Rabbi Sheila «came, they said to him: Why did you» order «flogging for this man? He said to them:» Because «he had relations with a female donkey.» According to Persian law this was an extremely heinous crime, so «they said to him: Do you have witnesses» that he did so? «He replied: Yes,» and «Elijah the prophet came» and «appeared as a person and testified. They said to» Rabbi Sheila: «If so, he is liable for the death penalty;» why did you not sentence him to death? «He replied: Since the day we were exiled from our land we do not have the authority to execute,» but «you, do with him as you wish.»

segments.he: עַד דִּמְעַיְּינִי בֵּיהּ בְּדִינָא, פְּתַח רַבִּי שֵׁילָא וַאֲמַר: ״לְךָ ה׳ הַגְּדֻלָּה וְהַגְּבוּרָה וְגוֹ׳״. אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: מַאי קָאָמְרַתְּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ, הָכִי קָאָמֵינָא: ״בְּרִיךְ רַחֲמָנָא דְּיָהֵיב מַלְכוּתָא בְּאַרְעָא כְּעֵין מַלְכוּתָא דִרְקִיעָא, וִיהַב לְכוּ שׁוּלְטָנָא וְרָחֲמִי דִּינָא״. אֲמַרוּ: חַבִּיבָא עֲלֵיהּ יְקָרָא דְמַלְכוּתָא כּוּלֵּי הַאי! יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ קוּלְפָא אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: דּוּן דִּינָא.
segments.en: «As» they «considered the sentence,» Rabbi Sheila praised God for saving him from danger: «“Yours, O Lord, is the greatness, power,» glory, triumph, and majesty; for all that is in heaven and on earth is Yours; Yours is the kingdom, O Lord, and You are exalted as head above all” (I Chronicles 29:11). «They asked him: What did you say? He told them: This is what I said: Blessed is Merciful One who grants kingdom on earth» that is a «microcosm of the kingdom in heaven, and granted you dominion and love of justice. They said to him:» Indeed, the «honor of royalty is so dear to you. They gave him a staff» to symbolize his license to sit in judgment and «said to him: Judge.»

segments.he: כִּי הֲוָה נָפֵיק, אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַהוּא גַּבְרָא: עָבֵיד רַחֲמָנָא נִיסָּא לְשַׁקָּרֵי הָכִי? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רָשָׁע, לָאו חֲמָרֵי אִיקְּרוּ? דִּכְתִיב: ״אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים בְּשָׂרָם״. חַזְיֵיהּ דְּקָאָזֵיל לְמֵימְרָא לְהוּ דִּקְרִינְהוּ חֲמָרֵי, אֲמַר: הַאי רוֹדֵף הוּא. וְהַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה: אִם בָּא לְהׇרְגְּךָ — הַשְׁכֵּם לְהׇרְגוֹ. מַחְיֵיהּ בְּקוּלְפָא וְקַטְלֵיהּ.
segments.en: «As he was leaving, that man said to» Rabbi Sheila: «Does God perform such miracles for liars? He replied: Scoundrel! Aren’t» gentiles «called donkeys? As it is written: “Whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys”» (Ezekiel 23:20). Rabbi Sheila «saw that he was going to tell» the Persian authorities «that he called them donkeys. He said:» This man has the legal status of «a pursuer.» He seeks to have me killed. «And the Torah said: If one comes to kill you, kill him first. He struck him with the staff and killed him.»

segments.he: אֲמַר: הוֹאִיל וְאִתְעֲבִיד לִי נִיסָּא בְּהַאי קְרָא, דָּרֵישְׁנָא לֵיהּ: ״לְךָ ה׳ הַגְּדֻלָּה״ — זוֹ מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״עֹשֶׂה גְדֹלוֹת עַד אֵין חֵקֶר״. ״וְהַגְּבוּרָה״ — זוֹ יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַיָּד הַגְּדֹלָה וְגוֹ׳״. ״וְהַתִּפְאֶרֶת״ — זוֹ חַמָּה וּלְבָנָה שֶׁעָמְדוּ לוֹ לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּדֹּם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְיָרֵחַ עָמָד וְגוֹ׳״. ״וְהַנֵּצַח״ — זוֹ מַפַּלְתָּהּ שֶׁל רוֹמִי. וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וְיֵז נִצְחָם עַל בְּגָדַי וְגוֹ׳״. ״וְהַהוֹד״ — זוֹ מִלְחֶמֶת נַחֲלֵי אַרְנוֹן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַל כֵּן יֵאָמַר בְּסֵפֶר מִלְחֲמֹת ה׳ אֶת וָהֵב בְּסוּפָה וְגוֹ׳״. ״כִּי כֹל בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ״ — זוֹ מִלְחֶמֶת סִיסְרָא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מִן שָׁמַיִם נִלְחָמוּ הַכּוֹכָבִים מִמְּסִלּוֹתָם וְגוֹ׳״. ״לְךָ ה׳ הַמַּמְלָכָה״ — זוֹ מִלְחֶמֶת עֲמָלֵק, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״כִּי יָד עַל כֵּס יָהּ״. ״וְהַמִּתְנַשֵּׂא״ — זוֹ מִלְחֶמֶת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״הִנְנִי אֵלֶיךָ גּוֹג נְשִׂיא רֹאשׁ מֶשֶׁךְ וְתֻבָל״. ״לְכֹל לְרֹאשׁ״ — אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֲפִילּוּ רֵישׁ גַּרְגִּיתָא מִן שְׁמַיָּא מַנּוּ לֵיהּ.
segments.en: Rabbi Sheila «said: Since a miracle was performed on my behalf with this verse» that I cited, «I will interpret it homiletically: Yours, O Lord, is the greatness; that is the act of creation, and so it says: “Who does great things past finding out”» (Job 9:10); «And the power; that is the exodus from Egypt, as it is stated: “And Israel saw the great work» which the Lord did to the «Egyptians”» (Exodus 14:31); «And the glory; that is the sun and the moon that stood still for Joshua, as it is stated: “And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed,» until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies” (Joshua 10:13); «And the triumph; that is the downfall of Rome, and so it says» describing the downfall of Edom, whom the Sages identified as the forefather of Rome: «“Their lifeblood is dashed against My garments» and I have stained all My raiment” (Isaiah 63:3); «And the majesty; this is the war of the valleys of Arnon, as it is stated: “Wherefore it is said in the book of the Wars of the Lord: Vahev in Sufa,» and the valleys of Arnon” (Numbers 21:14); «For all that is in the heaven and in the earth is Yours; this is the war of Sisera, as it is stated: “They fought from heaven, the stars in their courses» fought against Sisera” (Judges 5:20). «Yours is the kingdom, O Lord; this is the war of Amalek, and so it says:» “And he said: «The hand upon the throne of the Lord:» the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation” (Exodus 17:16), as then God will sit on His throne. «And you are exalted; this is the war of Gog and Magog, and so it says: “I am against you, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshekh and Tubal”» (Ezekiel 38:3); and: «As head above all; Rav Ḥanan bar Rava said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» All leadership and authority, «even» the most insignificant, the «one responsible for distributing water, is appointed by heaven.»

segments.he: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תַּנָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: ״לְךָ ה׳ הַגְּדֻלָּה״ — זוֹ קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף. ״וְהַגְּבוּרָה״ — זוֹ מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת. ״וְהַתִּפְאֶרֶת״ — זוֹ מַתַּן תּוֹרָה. ״וְהַנֵּצַח״ — זוֹ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם. ״וְהַהוֹד״ — זוֹ בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
segments.en: «It was taught in a baraita in the name of Rabbi Akiva:» «Yours, O Lord, is the greatness; this is the splitting of the Red Sea;» «the power; this is the plague of the firstborn;» «the glory; this is the giving of the Torah;» «the triumph; this is Jerusalem;» and «the majesty; this is the Temple.»

moves.cueHe: דרש רב המנונא
moves.summary: Rav Hamnuna teaches five distinct blessings for one who sees the ruins of wicked Babylonia.
moves.about: the five blessings recited on seeing the ruins of wicked Babylonia

moves.cueHe: רבא כי הוה חזי חמרי דשקלי עפרא
moves.summary: Rava urges on the donkeys carrying off Babylonian earth, enacting the occasion of the fifth blessing.
moves.about: Rava urging on the donkeys that carry off Babylonian earth

moves.cueHe: מר בריה דרבינא כי הוה מטי לבבל
moves.summary: Mar son of Ravina scatters Babylonian earth whenever he reaches Babylonia.
moves.about: Mar son of Ravina scattering Babylonian earth whenever he reached Babylonia

moves.cueHe: לקיים מה שנאמר ״וטאטאתיה במטאטא השמד״
moves.summary: Isaiah's 'broom of destruction' supplies the reason for that practice.
moves.about: the verse that Mar son of Ravina's practice fulfils

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אשי: אנא, הא דרב המנונא לא שמיע לי
moves.summary: Rav Ashi never received Rav Hamnuna's teaching yet recited all five blessings from his own reasoning.
moves.about: whether five blessings are recited on seeing Babylonia - Rav Ashi reached the same practice by his own reasoning, never having received Rav Hamnuna's teaching

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר: נתקללה בבל
moves.summary: Babylonia's curse dragged its neighbours down; Samaria's curse benefited hers.
moves.about: the prooftext that Babylonia's curse fell on its neighbours too

moves.cueHe: דכתיב: ״ושמתיה למורש קפד ואגמי מים״
moves.summary: Two verses ground each half of the contrast.
moves.about: the prooftext that Samaria's curse benefited its neighbours

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב המנונא: הרואה אוכלוסי ישראל
moves.summary: A further blessing of Rav Hamnuna: 'Knower of secrets' over multitudes of Israel, a verse of shame over multitudes of gentiles.
moves.about: the verse recited on seeing multitudes of gentiles

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן: הרואה אוכלוסי ישראל
moves.summary: A baraita states the same ruling and supplies its reason - no two minds or faces are alike.
moves.about: a Tosefta on the blessing over multitudes of Israel

moves.cueHe: בן זומא ראה אוכלוסא על גב מעלה בהר הבית
moves.summary: Ben Zoma adds a second blessing on seeing a multitude from a stair on the Temple Mount.
moves.about: why the sight of a multitude calls for blessing God as Knower of secrets - no two of them think or look alike

moves.cueHe: הוא היה אומר: כמה יגיעות יגע אדם הראשון
moves.summary: He explains the added blessing: Adam laboured through every stage for bread and clothing, while all of it is set ready before him.

moves.cueHe: הוא היה אומר: אורח טוב מהו אומר?
moves.summary: The good guest credits his host with everything; the bad guest discounts the trouble taken for him.

moves.cueHe: על אורח טוב מהו אומר? ״זכר כי תשגיא פעלו״
moves.summary: Two verses from Job voice the good and the bad guest.
moves.about: the verse that voices the good guest

moves.cueHe: ״והאיש בימי שאול זקן בא באנשים״
moves.summary: An associative turn to another verse about a man 'among men'.
moves.about: another verse containing the word 'among men', brought associatively on the theme of multitudes

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא, ואיתימא רב זביד, ואיתימא רב אושעיא: זה ישי אבי דוד
moves.summary: The man is Yishai, who always moved with a multitude; the tradition is alternatively attributed to Rav Zevid and Rav Oshaya.
moves.about: who the man who came among men in Saul's day was

moves.cueHe: אמר עולא: נקיטינן אין אוכלוסא בבבל
moves.summary: Ulla holds by tradition that there is no okhlosa in Babylonia.
moves.about: who said that the man who came among men is Yishai, father of David

moves.cueHe: תנא: אין אוכלוסא פחותה מששים ריבוא
moves.summary: A tanna fixes the threshold of an okhlosa at six hundred thousand.
moves.about: who said that the man who came among men is Yishai, father of David

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן: הרואה חכמי ישראל
moves.summary: A baraita gives the blessings on seeing Jewish and gentile sages and kings.
moves.about: the baraita on blessings over sages and kings, Jewish and gentile

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוחנן: לעולם ישתדל אדם לרוץ לקראת מלכי ישראל
moves.summary: One should run to greet even gentile kings, so as to be able to tell them apart hereafter.
moves.about: running out to greet kings, gentile kings included

moves.cueHe: רב ששת סגי נהור הוה
moves.summary: Blind Rav Sheshet joins the crowd going out to greet the king.
moves.about: denying that the king has arrived until the crowd falls silent

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: חצבי לנהרא, כגני לייא?
moves.summary: A heretic mocks him: what is a broken jug doing on the way to the river?
moves.about: what a blind man has to gain by going out to see the king

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: תא חזי דידענא טפי מינך
moves.summary: Rav Sheshet offers to show that he knows more than his sighted mocker.
moves.about: Rav Sheshet's claim that he knows more than his sighted mocker

moves.cueHe: חלף גונדא קמייתא
moves.summary: Through three troops he denies the king's arrival, and announces it only when silence falls.
moves.about: blind Rav Sheshet going out with everyone to greet the king

moves.cueHe: מנא לך הא?
moves.summary: The heretic asks how he knew.
moves.about: the source for knowing that the king comes in silence

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: דמלכותא דארעא כעין מלכותא דרקיעא
moves.summary: Earthly kingship is patterned on heavenly kingship.
moves.about: earthly kingship is patterned on heavenly kingship

moves.cueHe: דכתיב: ״צא ועמדת בהר לפני ה׳״
moves.summary: At Horeb God was not in wind, quake or fire but in the still small voice.
moves.about: God's revelation to Elijah at Horeb as the prooftext

moves.cueHe: כי אתא מלכא, פתח רב ששת וקא מברך ליה
moves.summary: The king arrives and Rav Sheshet blesses him.
moves.about: Rav Sheshet's gaze reducing the heretic to a heap of bones

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה ההוא מינא: למאן דלא חזית ליה קא מברכת?
moves.summary: Do you bless one you cannot see?
moves.about: how one can bless a king he cannot see

moves.cueHe: ומאי הוי עליה דההוא מינא?
moves.summary: The Gemara asks what became of the heretic.
moves.about: what ultimately became of that heretic

moves.cueHe: איכא דאמרי: חברוהי כחלינהו לעיניה
moves.summary: Two versions of his end are recorded side by side without deciding.
moves.about: two versions of the heretic's end, recorded without deciding between them

moves.summary: A second story on the link between earthly and heavenly kingship: Rabbi Sheila has an offender flogged.
moves.about: flogging a man who had relations with a gentile woman

moves.cueHe: אזל אכל ביה קורצי בי מלכא
moves.summary: The man denounces him to the royal court for judging without the king's licence.
moves.about: informing the royal court that Rabbi Sheila judges without the king's authority

moves.cueHe: מאי טעמא נגדתיה להאי?
moves.summary: The court asks why he had the man flogged.
moves.about: why he had the man flogged

moves.cueHe: אמר להו: דבא על חמרתא
moves.summary: He answers that the man had relations with a female donkey - a capital offence in Persian law.
moves.about: the charge on which the man was flogged

moves.cueHe: אמרי ליה: אית לך סהדי?
moves.summary: Have you witnesses?
moves.about: whether he has witnesses to the charge

moves.cueHe: אתא אליהו אדמי ליה כאיניש, ואסהיד
moves.summary: Elijah appears in human form and testifies.
moves.about: Elijah appearing in human form and testifying for Rabbi Sheila before the court

moves.cueHe: אמרי ליה: אי הכי, בר קטלא הוא!
moves.summary: Then he was liable to death - why was he only flogged?
moves.about: why he only flogged a man whose offence carries the death penalty

moves.cueHe: אמר להו: אנן מיומא דגלינן מארעין לית לן רשותא למקטל
moves.summary: Since the exile the Jewish court has no power of execution; do with him as you wish.
moves.about: since the exile the Jewish court has no authority to execute

moves.cueHe: פתח רבי שילא ואמר: ״לך ה׳ הגדלה והגבורה וגו׳״
moves.summary: While the court deliberates he recites the Chronicles verse in praise of God.
moves.about: the verse he recited in praise while the court deliberated

moves.cueHe: אמרי ליה: מאי קאמרת?
moves.summary: They ask what he said.
moves.about: what the words he had just recited meant

moves.cueHe: אמר להו, הכי קאמינא
moves.summary: He renders it as a blessing of God who granted an earthly kingdom patterned on the heavenly one.
moves.about: he glosses his recitation as a blessing of God who granted an earthly kingdom modelled on the heavenly one

moves.cueHe: אמרו: חביבא עליה יקרא דמלכותא כולי האי!
moves.summary: They praise his devotion to royal honour and give him a staff with licence to judge.
moves.about: his devotion to the honour of the kingdom

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה ההוא גברא: עביד רחמנא ניסא לשקרי הכי?
moves.summary: Does God work such miracles for liars?
moves.about: whether God performs miracles for liars, since the charge Rabbi Sheila gave the court was false

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: רשע, לאו חמרי איקרו?
moves.summary: Gentiles are themselves called donkeys, as Ezekiel says, so the testimony was no lie.
moves.about: gentiles are themselves called donkeys, so the charge was no lie

moves.cueHe: חזייה דקאזיל למימרא להו דקרינהו חמרי, אמר: האי רודף הוא
moves.summary: Seeing the man going to report him, he treats him as a pursuer and kills him with the staff.
moves.about: calling him a scoundrel for the accusation

moves.cueHe: אמר: הואיל ואתעביד לי ניסא בהאי קרא, דרישנא ליה

moves.about: each clause of 'Yours, O Lord, is the greatness' designates a distinct divine act, from creation to Gog and Magog

moves.cueHe: ״לכל לראש״ — אמר רב חנן בר רבא אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: The closing clause, in Rabbi Yohanan's name: even the officer of the water ditch is appointed from heaven.
moves.about: the reading of 'as head above all' as covering even the humblest appointment

moves.cueHe: במתניתא תנא משמיה דרבי עקיבא
